To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the PKB PH-domain has a high affinity for 3-phosphorylated phosphoinositide ligands; (2) the PKB-PtdIns(4.5)P(,2) complex is unstable; (3) inositol phosphatases can be bound by PKB, but only in a flipped orientation with respect to the other 3-phosphoinositide ligand.
the inositol ring of Ins(1,3,4,6)P(4) is flipped with respect the inositol rings of Ins(1)P(3), Ins(3)P(3).
the in vivo selectivity of the PKB pleckstrin domain for 3 phosphorylation is due to a preference for the orientation of the inositol ring in the 3 phosphorylation state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational models that help us to understand the molecular basis of the interactions of the PH domain of PKB with phosphoinositide head groups.

the development of computational models that can successfully reproduce in vivo data, as well as with the identification of new binding modes for the PKB PH that could explain some of its unexpected experimental results.
understanding the relative affinity and selectivity of PKB's PH domain for inositol phosphate lipid head groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our computational results suggest that the PKB PH is a relatively promiscuous domain, which binds to 3 phosphorylated and 2 phosphorylated phosphoinositol head groups with similar affinity.

the in vivo selectivity of the PKB-PH domain for 3 phosphorylation of inositol phospholipid head groups is due to a combination of the electrostatics of the phosphate head group, the hydrophobic effect, and the conformational dynamics of the inositol ring, and the inositol-phosphate head group.

the PKB PH binds inositol phosphate rings in a flipped orientation when the inositol ring does not carry a phosphatidyl tail and binds the inositol head group in the canonical orientation when the inositide ring is bonded to the phosphatidyl group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our computational models provide a detailed understanding of the binding mode of the PKB pleckstrin PH domain with inositol phospholipids.

we have used molecular dynamics simulations to understand the relative affinity and selectivity of the PKB pleckstrin domain for inositol phosphate-containing ligands, with particular focus on inositol 3 phosphorylation and the role of the phosphatidate head group.
the inositol ring orientation is an important determinant of binding affinity for the PKB PH.
The main takeaway from our work is that

computational models can help to rationalize the unexpected in vitro binding data of PKB with Ins(1, 4, 5)P(,3), and to better understand the molecular details of the binding of PKB with the inosiol phosphate head groups involved in the PI 3 kinase pathway.
the inositol ring of the inositol head group of phosphoinositide ligands is a critical determinant of PKB PH domain binding, whereas the phosphate groups are of lesser importance.
the PH domain of PKB is able to bind to a wide range of different phosphoinositide head groups, but that its in vivo specificity is dictated by the phosphatidate tails of the phosphoinositides.
